Johnson 3. Fast-acting smart inverters that utilize preset operating conditions to determine real and reactive power injection/consumption can create voltage instabilities (over-voltage, voltage oscillations and more) in an electrical distribution network if set-points are not properly configured.

arxiv-2112-13162.title: Stealthy Attack on Algorithmic-Protected DNNs via Smart Bit Flipping
arxiv-2112-13162.creator: Behnam Ghavami, Seyd Movi, Zhenman Fang, Lesley Shannon
arxiv-2112-13162.description: Abstract Recently, deep neural networks (DNNs) have been deployed in safety-critical systems such as autonomous vehicles and medical devices. Shortly after that, the vulnerability of DNNs were revealed by stealthy adversarial examples where crafted inputs—by adding tiny perturbations to original inputs—can lead a DNN to generate misclassification outputs.

arxiv-2205-13406.title: Differentially Private Formation Control: Privacy and Network Co-Design
arxiv-2205-13406.creator: Calvin Hawkins, Matthew Hale
arxiv-2205-13406.description: Abstract As multi-agent systems proliferate, there is increasing need for coordination protocols that protect agents’ sensitive information while still allowing them to collaborate. Often, a network system and controller are first designed and implemented, and then privacy is only incorporated after that.

arxiv-2205-14520.title: Transfer Learning as a Method to Reproduce High-Fidelity NLTE Opacities in Simulations
arxiv-2205-14520.creator: Michael D. Vander Wal, Ryan G. McClarren, Kelli D. Humbird
arxiv-2205-14520.description: Abstract Simulations of high-energy density physics often need non-local thermodynamic equilibrium (NLTE) opacity data. This data, however, is expensive to produce at relatively low-fidelity. It is even more so at high-fidelity such that the opacity calculations can contribute ninety-five percent of the total computation time. This proportion can even reach large proportions.

arxiv-2209-09971.title: Prevalence of mutualism in a simple model of microbial co-evolution
arxiv-2209-09971.creator: Luciano Stucchi, Javier Galeano, Juan Manuel Pastor, Jose María Iriondo, José A. Cuesta
arxiv-2209-09971.description: Abstract Evolutionary transitions among ecological interactions are widely known, although their detailed dynamics remain absent for most population models. Adaptive dynamics has been used to illustrate how the parameters of population models might shift through evolution, but within an ecological regime.

arxiv-2311-15428.title: The Pickup and Delivery Problem with Crossdock for Perishable Goods
arxiv-2311-15428.creator: Konstantinos Gkiotsalitis, Amalia Nikolopoulou
arxiv-2311-15428.description: Abstract Our work departs from the original definition of the Pickup and Delivery Problem (PDP) and extends it by considering an interchange point (crossdock) where vehicles can exchange their goods with other vehicles in order to shorten their delivery routes and reduce their running times.

arxiv-2405-06730.title: Ocean-DC: An analysis ready data cube framework for environmental and climate change monitoring over the port areas
arxiv-2405-06730.creator: Ioannis Kavouras, Ioannis Rallis, Nikolaos Doulamis, Anastasios Doulamis
arxiv-2405-06730.description: Abstract The environmental hazards and climate change effects causes serious problems in land and coastal areas. A solution to this problem can be the periodic monitoring over critical areas, like coastal region with heavy industrial activity (i.e., ship-buildings) or areas where a disaster (i.e., oil-spill) has occurred.

pmc-10563139.title: Obtaining Pure 1H NMR Spectra of Individual Pyranose and Furanose Anomers of Reducing Deoxyfluorinated Sugars
pmc-10563139.creator: Gabija Poškaitė, David E Wheatley, Neil Wells, Bruno Linclau, Davy Sinnaeve
pmc-10563139.description: Due to tautomeric equilibria, NMR spectra of reducing sugars can be complex with many overlapping resonances. This hampers coupling constant determination, which is required for conformational analysis and configurational assignment of substituents. Given that mixtures of interconverting species are physically inseparable, easy-to-use techniques that enable facile full 1H NMR characterization of sugars are of interest.

pmc-11352891.title: The Loss of PPARγ Expression and Signaling Is a Key Feature of Cutaneous Actinic Disease and Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Association with Tumor Stromal Inflammation
pmc-11352891.creator: Raymond L. Konger, Xiaoling Xuei, Ethel Derr-Yellin, Fang Fang, Hongyu Gao, Yunlong Liu
pmc-11352891.description: Given the importance of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR)-gamma in epidermal inflammation and carcinogenesis, we analyzed the transcriptomic changes observed in epidermal PPARγ-deficient mice (Pparg-/-epi). A gene set enrichment analysis revealed a close association with epithelial malignancy, inflammatory cell chemotaxis, and cell survival.

pmc-12639539.title: Sodium bicarbonate to the ROSCue: a case report on how sodium bicarbonate successfully resuscitated a patient in cardiac arrest from suspected quetiapine and trazodone overdose
pmc-12639539.creator: Madhumita Kolluri, Jennifer Callaghan, Joel Wilken, Jason Gluck, Felix Wiedmann, Dzan Horozic, Evan Schreyer, Faris Kadíc
pmc-12639539.description: BackgroundPer ACLS algorithms (Class III, LOE B), sodium bicarbonate (SB) use is indicated for cardiac arrest with underlying hyperkalaemia, tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) overdose, or pre-existing severe metabolic acidosis, with routine use of SB being discouraged due to concerns raised in animal studies.

pmc-13133645.title: Refining the Role of ERK Signaling in Anthracycline-Induced Cardiotoxicity
pmc-13133645.creator: Zheyu Wang, Defeng Zhao
pmc-13133645.description: ation. The first concerns the observation that homozygous erk1−/− mutants develop intrinsic cardiac dysfunction and aggravate anthracycline toxicity despite reduced senescence. This finding implies that basal ERK activity is indispensable for short-term cardiomyocyte survival. The need for basal ERK signaling appears to outweigh the potential benefit of attenuating long-term cellular aging.

pmc-13392192.title: FZD7 Inhibitor SRI Attenuates High Glucose‐Induced Retinal Pigment Epithelial Cell Injury Accompanied by Ferroptosis‐Associated Changes via Suppression of the Wnt/β‐Catenin Pathway
pmc-13392192.creator: Jiaojiao Jiang, Liu Zheng, Liwu Tan, Zhixiang Ding
pmc-13392192.description: PurposeThis study investigated the protective effects of the Frizzled‐7 (FZD7) inhibitor SRI against high glucose–induced injury in human retinal pigment epithelial (ARPE‐19) cells. It also explored the underlying mechanism, focusing on whether SRI attenuates ferroptosis and apoptosis by inhibiting the Wnt/β‐catenin signalling pathway.

pmc-13570330.title: Supercritical Solution Impregnation: A Strategy to Prevent Prosthetic Infections
pmc-13570330.creator: Andrea Salas, Sara Díaz, Eduardo Pérez, Helga K. Ruiz, Rama Hafian, Pablo Sanz, Lourdes Calvo, Albertina Cabañas
pmc-13570330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). One of the most devastating and frustrating complications in orthopaedic surgery is infection. A project is underway in our laboratory to explore the use of supercritical CO2 (scCO2) as an impregnation medium for treating orthopaedic prostheses to prevent infections. We present our results on the incorporation of antibiotics into the polymeric part of prostheses (inserts) using scCO2 as a green solvent capable of penetrating the inserts carrying the drug without altering their structural integrity.
